text.0_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) HE CALLED TO MOSHE.  Always from inside the cloud, as on Mt. Sinai, as it says (Exod. 24:16), "On the seventh day He called Moshe from the midst of the cloud," for he could never enter there without permission.
text.0_Chapter, 0_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) FROM THE TENT OF MEETING.  For Moshe did not enter the Tent of Meeting while the Glory was still there.  This was on the day when Moshe finished erecting the Mishkan, for it was then that the Glory descended to sanctify the place and its attendants as it says (Exod. 29:43-44), "and there I will meet with the Israelites, and it shall be sanctified by My Presence. I will sanctify the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and Aaron and his sons ...."  He did the same thing with Shlomo's Temple, as it says (I Kings 8:11), "the priests were not able to remain and perform the service because of the cloud, for the Presence of Adonai filled the House of Adonai."  And in this way, He sanctified the place, as it says (I Kings 9:3), "I consecrate this House that you have built."  However, from the first day on, Moshe entered the Tent of Meeting outside the curtain, as it says (Num. 7:89), "When Moshe went into the Tent of Meeting to speak with Him, he would hear the Voice addressing him from above the [Ark] cover ...."
text.0_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) A PERSON WHEN HE OFFERS, FROM AMONG YOU [JPS: WHEN ANY OF YOU PRESENTS AN OFFERING].  When he offers from yourselves, through verbal confession and humbling, as with (Hos. 14:3), "Instead of bulls we will pay [The offering of] our lips," and as it says (Ps. 51:19), "True sacrifice to God is a contrite spirit."  For there is no need for fools who sacrifice without first having humbled themselves.  And the Sages have already said, "from among you and not all of you, to exclude the apostate.
text.0_Chapter, 1_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) FROM THE BEASTS.  If he offers from the beasts, it should only be from the herd or from the flock, and not any wild animal, even if it is within the category of beast, as it says (Deut. 14:4-5), "These are the animals that you may eat: ... the deer, the gazelle, ...."  The intent in these sections is to specify the categories who bring sacrifices, the categories of things sacrificed, the categories of sacrifices, and the reasons for sacrificing.  It specifies that voluntary sacrifices are accepted from any person, even from the nations, as it clarifies later on, in saying (Lev. 22:25), "nor shall you accept such [animals] from a foreigner for offering as food for your God, for they are mutilated, they have a defect."  And after all, apostates are lower than Gentiles, in particular, apostates to idolatry and to public desecration of Shabbat.  And it specifies that the kinds of animals that are sacrificed are the herd and the flock among the beasts, turtle doves and pigeons among the birds, and fine flour, oil, and frankincense.  And it specifies that the kinds of sacrifices are the burnt offering, the sacrifice of well-being, and the flour offering. all of which are sometimes voluntary, and the sin offering and the guilt offering, which are always obligatory.  And from this there is clarification of the matter of Kayin -- its saying (Gen. 4:5). "but to Kayin and his offering He paid no attention," for he [Kayin] was among the group of sectarians, from whom we do not accept sacrifices, as the end of the story clarifies the beginning, for his offering was of a species that is inappropriate for  sacrifice.  Similarly with Noah, when it says (Gen. 8:21), "Adonai smelled the pleasing odor," it says that He accepted the portion of his sacrifices that would make a pleasing odor, it being from a species that was appropriate for sacrifice.  But He did not accept all of his offering, because it included all pure species and all pure birds.  And there can also be understood from this what is said (Ps. 40:7), "You gave me to understand that You do not desire sacrifice and grain offering," and also what is said (Isa. 1:11), "What need have I of all your sacrifices?," and many such statements in Holy Scriptures.  For it is indeed appropriate that the one who brings the sacrifice be one who is fit to bring, that he choose a species that is appropriate to offer and that is calculated to achieve the result for purposes of which he brought the sacrifice, and that he should lay his hands on the sacrifice as does a supplicant, and pray that his sin rest on the head of the sacrifice, as with the scapegoat.  And in this way he will to some extent turn the thought of repentance that is in his mind into the actual practice of humility: "that it may be acceptable on his behalf, in expiation for him" (v.4).  Since some of the sins are in thought alone and some are also in deed, what is appropriate to atone for the mental component is that portion that ascends in fire on the altar, those being the burnt offering, the limbs of [other] offerings, and the token portion of the flour offerings [that is burnt], and what is appropriate to atone for the deeds will be the portions given to the priests.  Thus, corresponding to the limbs of the sinner, which engaged in evil acts, parts of the limbs of the sacrifice will be given to God's servants, who engage in His worship, as it says (Lev. 10:17), "it is what was given to you to remove the guilt of the community and to make expiation for them."  And so the Sages said that the priests eat and the owners [of the sacrifice] have atonement made.  And when the bad deed for which atonement is to be made through a sacrifice is partly of a serious gravity like liability for karet, and partly less serious than that, though still with some desecration of sanctity, a sin offering (hatat) is appropriate for the first part, to cleanse (l'hatei) the soul polluted with liability for karet, as it says, "that person [nefesh] shall be cut off [nich'r'ta]."  And for the second part, a guilt offering is appropriate, to remove the desecration for which he is guilty, this being done by the humbling, through the sacrifice with the repentance, and the rule [that the priests eat the sacrifice] applies to both of them [sin offering and the guilt offering].  However, the sacrifice of well-being [which is eaten by the priests but does not atone for sin] links the owners with God's servants, to worship Him equally.
text.9_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) AHARON'S SONS EACH TOOK HIS FIRE PAN.  They thought that, just as after the daily sacrifice, on which God would rest His presence, as it is said (Exod. 29:42), "a regular burnt offering throughout the generations, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting before GOD, where I will meet with you," there would come the incense, thus it would be appropriate to offer new incense now for the revelation of Adonai's glory to all of the people, and for the descent of the fire, and that is why they offered this.
text.9_Chapter, 0_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) BEFORE ADONAI.   On the inside altar, about which it is said (Exod. 30:9). "You shall not offer alien incense on it."  And even if it would have been appropriate to act this way had they been commanded to do so, they sinned in doing so now.
text.9_Chapter, 0_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) WHICH HAD NOT BEEN ENJOINED UPON THEM.  As the Sages said, they issued halachic rulings in the face of Moshe their master.
text.9_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: AND AHARON WAS SILENT.  He consoled himself with the Sanctification of God that had been effected through their death.
text.11_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: ON THE EIGHTH DAY THERE SHALL BE CIRCUMCISED.  For then the niddah blood, with which the fetus has been sustained in its mother's womb, will be absorbed, and the fetus will be  pure so as to enter into the covenant of holiness.
text.11_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: IN THE STATE OF BLOOD PURIFICATION.  For even though it is niddah blood, it is not from this menstruation, but is rather from the previous menstruations, during her pregnancy, for the form of the bloods of those menstruations and their impurities has been spoiled and ruined.
text.11_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: TWO WEEKS.  Because the excesses increase in the birth of a female.
text.11_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: MAKE EXPIATION.  Because during the entire time of her impure flow, all of her thoughts will turn to matters of impurity relating to seed, so she will not be fit for the Temple and its sancta until she brings her expiation and turns toward the holy.
text.15_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: ADONAI SPOKE TO MOSHE AFTER THE DEATH.  The word "vay'daber" in Hebrew generally does not apply to specific things said, but rather applies to the process of speaking in general.  Thus, after the expression "dibur" (speaking) generally comes the specific expression "amirah" (saying).  Thus, it says, "Adonai spoke to Moshe after the death ... and He said to him, 'Speak to Aharon your brother.'"  And because it goes on at length in recounting "after the death," it does not say "He said to him," but instead goes back and mentions God, may He be blessed, the sayer, and Moshe the hearer.  However, according to some of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, there were two statements, and the structure of the passage would be, "Adonai spoke to Moshe and said to him, 'Speak to Aharon that he not come and not die,' and after the death of Aharon's two sons, He said to Moshe, 'Speak to Aharon that he not come'" -- that he not enter more than he was commanded -- "'and that he not die -- as his sons died when they broke through to offer incense more than they were commanded'" -- and this would prod him more than the first.
text.15_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: FOR I APPEAR IN THE CLOUD in this generation to speak to Moshe, but in other generations to call to those prepared for prophecy, as was the case with Shmu'el, as it says (I Sam. 3:3-4), "Shmu'el was sleeping in the temple of Adonai, where the Ark of God was, and Adonai called out to Shmu'el.
text.15_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: THIS IS HOW [AHARON] SHALL ENTER ... WITH A BULL OF THE HERD.  By consecrating a bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, and wearing linen garments, which have no color and no artificial decoration.  For indeed, the High Priest must not delay entering the sanctuary until after the sacrifice of the burnt offering, but should enter to offer the incense immediately after the slaughtering of the sin offering.
text.15_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: TWO HE-GOATS FOR SIN OFFERING.  The first for the sins committed in the sanctuary, and the scapegoat for the other sins of the community, and, because of the magnitude of its impurity, it is not fit for slaughtering, and it would make the one who accompanies it impure.
text.15_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: LOTS.  For the lot, specifically by His faithful one (Deut. 33:8), is [used] when one asks a question of God, as it says (Prov. 16:33), "Lots are cast into the lap; The decision depends on Adonai.".
text.15_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: AND MAKES IT A SIN OFFERING.  The lot makes the goat a sin offering, as [the Sages] said, "The lot makes the sin offering, and [the calling of] the name does not make a sin offering.
text.18_Chapter, 13_Verse, 0_Comment: At this point the Torah warns that one must not cause distress to one’s fellow man by undermining his dignity, his self image and the image he enjoys among his peers. Example are: לא תקלל חרש, this is a damage that the deaf person does not even become aware of. Next, the Torah discusses tangible damages, such as
text.18_Chapter, 13_Verse, 1_Comment: לפני עור לא תתן מכשול, indirect damages, for who knows if the blind will trip over the obstacle? The one causing even indirect damage is held responsible by the Torah. [this is presumably in the realm of heavenly judgment, seeing that the Talmud feels that people, as opposed to animals, who have eyes in their head, should watch out for obstacles in their path. Ed.]
text.20_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) ADONAI SAID TO MOSHE, SAY TO THE PRIESTS.  What was said above -- to understand and to instruct regarding all sorts of impurities, to distinguish between the pure and impure domestic beasts and between the pure and impure birds, for this is more appropriate for the priests, according to what He said, "to distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the pure and  the impure."
text.20_Chapter, 0_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) AND SAY TO THEM.  That they must refrain not only from these, but also from the impurity of a corpse and from profaning their seed, for these are qualities of holiness applicable to the priests alone.  ...
text.20_Chapter, 0_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) HE SHALL NOT BECOME IMPURE FOR A [DEAD] PERSON AMONG HIS KIN.  No one among the priests shall become impure for a [dead] person among "his people" -- i.e., any dead person among the multitudes who is not among his relatives, but is simply "from his people."
text.20_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: A CHIEF SHALL NOT BECOME IMPURE FOR ONE AMONG HIS PEOPLE [JPS:  BUT HE SHALL NOT DEFILE HIMSELF AS A KINSMAN BY MARRIAGE] AND SO PROFANE HIMSELF.  And the reason why the priest must not become impure except for his relatives is that the priest is in fact "a chief among his people" to understand and to instruct, "for the lips of a priest guard knowledge, And rulings are sought from his mouth" (Mal. 2:7).  And it is appropriate for a person like this to comport himself like a prince "so that his words will be heeded," and it is not appropriate to profane his eligibility for the Sanctuary and its appurtenances to honor dead persons who are not his relatives, as they said (Sanh. 47a), that the burial and the eulogy for the dead person are "honor to the deceased" [as opposed to being honor to the mourners].  However, for relatives, [the Torah] permits becoming impure, for the honor to them is an honor to him.
text.20_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: THEY SHALL NOT SHAVE.  Even though I have allowed them impurity for their dead for their own honor, I have not allowed them to be extreme in their mourning to increase the honor to their dead by shaving and scarifying, as they, z"l, said (Sifra, ch. 1:3), "just as there it is over the dead, so here it is over the dead."
text.20_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: THEY SHALL NOT PROFANE THE NAME OF THEIR GOD.  Even though all of these are for the sake of his honor, he is not entitled to forgo his honor, for in fact the point of the honor of the priests is for the honor of God, may He be blessed, and when they forgo this, they desecrate His name.
text.20_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: FOR HE IS HOLY TO HIS [JPS: THEY ARE HOLY TO THEIR] GOD.  Each descendant of the priesthood, being a chief among his people, is holy to his God, and if he marries these women, he will profane his honor and his seed, who will not be fit for that holiness.
text.24_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: ADONAI SPOKE TO MOSHE ON MT. SINAI.  Now [the Torah] does not mention the location of the command in the case of any mitzva unless something new happened in that place, but [here] it clarifies that when God, may He be exalted, said on Sinai (Ex. 23:11), "in the seventh you shall let it rest and lie fallow. Let the needy among your people eat of it, etc..," He then explained to Moshe all the laws the laws of the seventh year that are stated in this place, to understand and to instruct.  And this itself was [the case] for all other mitzvot, for even though, in some of their cases, what was said was only brief Scripture, the clarification then was expansive, with great clarity.  As they, z"l, said, "What is the relevance of Sh'mita to Mr.Sinai? But just as, in the case of Sh'mita, its general rules, explanations, and details were spoken on Sinai, so all the other mitzvot -- their general rules, explanations, and details were spoken on Sinai.  And Moshe our Teacher mentions this section in this place because he thought that they would immediately be entering the land, as he testified when he said (Num. 10:29), "we are setting out for the place."  And he enjoined them regarding the sh'mita of the soil in particular because it was from their sin regarding its observance that they would be exiled from it, as it testifies in saying (Lev. 26:34), "Then shall the land make up for its sabbath years," and it testifies similarly at the end of Chronicles, in saying (II Chron. 26:21), "until the land paid back its sabbaths."
text.24_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) WHEN YOU ENTER THE LAND.  The "Galilee of the Nations" (Isa. 8:23).
text.24_Chapter, 1_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) THE LAND SHALL REST.  The soil that is ready for the work of the land.
text.24_Chapter, 1_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) A SABBATH OF ADONAI.  That the whole year that is idle from working the land will be ready for service to Him, as He intended regarding Shabbat, as He said (Exod. 20:10), "a Shabbat of Adonai your God."
text.24_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) SIX YEARS YOU CAN [JPS: MAY] SOW YOUR FIELD.  Then you will be able to sow a single field, through its strength, six years in a row, which is contrary to the principles of farming, for in fact the custom regarding it is that it should be fallow one year and he should sow it one year, as our Rabbis mentioned.
text.24_Chapter, 2_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) YOU WILL GATHER ITS YIELD.  Contrary to the custom in farming, that, if they sow its portion in its strength for consecutive years, it will not continue to yield its strength.
text.24_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) THE LAND SHALL HAVE A SABBATH OF COMPLETE REST.  Even from merely preparatory farmwork, like placing manure on [cut] trees, smearing oil [on pruned trees], perforating unripe fruit, and the sort, that they, z"l, mentioned.  ...
text.24_Chapter, 3_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) A SABBATH OF ADONAI.  Also the farm workers, when they rest that year, will be aroused to seek Adonai in some way.
text.25_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) IF YOU FOLLOW [LIT.: WALK IN] MY LAWS.  "Hukot" are Royal decrees in accordance with which one is to conduct oneself in pursuing the affairs of one's life.  And the conducting oneself in accordance with them is called "walking," as it is said (Lev. 18:3), "Do not follow [lit. walk in] their laws," and likewise (Lev. 18:4), "Keep my laws, following [lit., walking in] them," and similarly (Ezek. 33:15), "follow [lit. walk in] the laws of life."
text.25_Chapter, 2_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) AND OBSERVE MY COMMANDMENTS.  "Observing" with respect to commandments is the attention to the manner of doing them and to their purpose, and with appropriate deliberation, as [the Sages] said, "'Observe' -- that means study."  It says, therefore, that if you conduct yourself in accordance with the ways of God, may He be blessed, that are included in the practical portion of His Torah, and you deliberate about the commandments so as to know the manner of doing them and their purpose, then you will thereby fulfill their purpose of your being in His image and His likeness.
text.25_Chapter, 2_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) AND DO THEM.  And then you will have this complete acquisition, in the manner that you will do them like workers for the good, with a willing spirit, and not like those who are commanded and comply out of fear, such that the one who performs is compelled to some degree.  Rather, perform from love, seeking the good will of God, may He be blessed, as [the Sages] said, "Do His will like your own will."
text.25_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) OLD GRAIN LONG STORED.  After there remain only a smaller number of Gentiles, who will be your farmers and grape growers, the grain harvest will be greater, with one year's [harvest] lasting for several years, so that the few remaining Gentiles will suffice to serve you by gathering your produce, and besides this, you will be provided for without difficulty, as in (Ps. 72:16), "Let abundant grain be in the land, to the tops of the mountains; let his crops thrive like the forest of Lebanon," and, as [the Sages] said in the last chapter of Ketubot, "In the future, the Land of Israel will produce cakes and woolen garments.
text.25_Chapter, 9_Verse, 1_Comment: (2)  AND YOU SHALL HAVE TO CLEAR OUT THE OLD TO MAKE ROOM FOR THE NEW.  What you have from your old crop will suffice for your needs, even though since the old crop still exists, you can export some of it to provide for the remnant of the nations, as it says (Isa. 60:12), "For the nation or the kingdom that does not serve you shall perish."  And the reason that you will be able to export something having life-giving sustenance from your land to the nations is that the new crop will have come in, and you will not worry that there will not be enough for you, as was the case when [the Sages] said, "One may not export from the Land of Israel something having life-giving sustenance, such as wine, oil, or flours."
